# Radoslav Radev Advises Always Starting The Workout With The Hardest Progression

Radoslav Radev advises always starting the workout with the hardest progression and the highest goal, when the nervous system is fresh after the warm-up. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 02:25]

## Details

- Do your hardest attempts first, not conditioning exercises or easier exercises. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 02:36]
- If you do successful attempts in the beginning of the workout with better hold and better progress, you can even stop the workout after 30 minutes if you achieved a record or the next progression. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 02:52]
- Training efficiently and putting focus on the right thing means that with 100 workouts per year, each workout you achieve something: one second more, one rep more, better technique, next progression. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 03:25]
- You can progress faster with 30-minute workouts four times per week than someone training six or seven times per week for two hours with no progress. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 03:25]

## Evidence

- vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 02:25 (Radoslav Radev): "rule number two always start with the hardest progression and the hardest thing that you want to achieve your highest focus your fresh nervous system your best strength is actually in the beginning of your workout after the warm-up"
- vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 02:36 (Radoslav Radev): "do your hardest attempts first always don't do the conditioning exercises or exercises for front lever plunge [planche] or handstand or whatever you train exercises and attempt first never"
- vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 02:52 (Radoslav Radev): "if you do in the beginning of the workout successful attempts more hold better progress like never before next progression better technique if you want you can stop the workout you can trade 30 minutes if you achieve better result like never before some record or go to the next progression"
- vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 03:25 (Radoslav Radev): "imagine you have 100 workouts for the year and every workout you're achieving something else like one second more one rep more better technique next progression you can just do 30 minutes workout four times per week and you can progress much faster than someone could train six seven times per week two hours and not having any progress"
